territorial_scope.description: Designation applies to the Apple undertaking's provision of the Mobile Platform digital activity, which the decision finds linked to the UK; it is addressed to named Apple entities.

evidence.quote: we are designating Apple as having SMS in the provision of its Mobile Platform with effect from the date of this decision.

summary.short: The UK Competition and Markets Authority designates Apple as having strategic market status in its Mobile Platform (iOS, iPadOS, App Store, Safari, WebKit) under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, effective 22 October 2025 for five years. No conduct requirements are imposed.
summary.long: The CMA decides under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 that Apple has strategic market status (SMS) in a single grouped digital activity, the Mobile Platform. It covers the Smartphone and Tablet Operating Systems (iOS, iPadOS), Native App Distribution (the App Store) and the Mobile Browser and Browser Engine (Safari and WebKit), linked to the UK. The designated undertaking comprises Apple Inc. and Apple Distribution International Limited. The decision finds that the turnover condition is met (global turnover above £25 billion or UK turnover above £1 billion, either sufficing) and that Apple has substantial and entrenched market power and a position of strategic significance. Designation takes effect from the decision date and lasts five years, subject to review or revocation. The decision imposes no conduct requirements; any such measures would require separate processes and further public consultation. It states that it does not find wrongdoing. Pre-installation, sideloading and web apps are excluded from the activity descriptions, and developer tools fall within Native App Distribution only where they fit its description.

notes: Part 1 of 4 (paras 1.1-5.15 and footnotes). Relations drawn from this part only; no registry IDs assumed, so target_instrument_id is empty. Non-registry materials (CMA guidance CMA194, CMA reports, Explanatory Notes) are cited as cross-references, not legal bases. Figures are partly redacted ([] and ranges). Inconsistency: Safari's share on iOS is 84% for June 2025 (footnote 277) but 86%, described as consistent for many years, in footnote 241 and Appendix A. Part 2 of 4 (paragraphs 5.16 to 6.130, chapters 5 and 6; appendices not included). Relations are limited to instruments cited in this part. The Act is cited only by section number and as 'the Act', so target_instrument_id is blank. CMA194 is cited by paragraph number only and is not identified here. Internal inconsistencies: para. 6.38 gives 9% switched, 11% considered, 81% did not consider for all users, which sums to 101%. Footnote 376 reads 'Google’s and Google’s Mobile Ecosystems', presumably meaning Apple’s and Google’s. Many figures are redacted ([✄]) or given as bracketed ranges. Only relations and notes are annotated for this part. Part 3 of 4 (paras 6.131 to 8.37). Relations stated here are citations only: the Act is named only as 'the Act', CMA194 only by number, and other CMA decisions and reports in footnotes. No amendment, repeal or legal-basis statement appears in this part. Many passages are redacted ([✄]). Labelling inconsistency: para 8.4 lists sub-item (c) before (a) and (b). Footnote 582 refers to 'the Guidance' without naming CMA194 in this part. The text refers to an earlier 'Proposed Decision' stage; this part does not say whether the instrument is that decision's final version. Part 4 of 4 covers paras 8.40 to 8.96 (market, technological and regulatory developments; substantial and entrenched market power; position of strategic significance). Relations are limited to external instruments cited in this part; the Act is referred to only by its short form. Text inconsistencies: para 8.59 lists items (d) to (f) with no (a) to (c); para 8.87 contains a doubled full stop ('not continue..'). Many figures are redacted, shown as '[✄] [range]' (e.g., para 8.70(a), 8.71), and the ranges are the text's own bracketed values.

thresholds.measurement: Turnover in the relevant period: the most recent 12-month period for which the CMA can estimate relevant turnover, or an earlier 12-month period if higher (para. 3.11); CMA estimates turnover; for groups, the whole group is considered (fn. 64).
thresholds.consequence: Turnover condition met in relation to the undertaking; the CMA may designate it as having SMS only if the turnover condition is met.
thresholds.conditions: Alternative to the UK turnover threshold (either suffices); the substantial and entrenched market power and position of strategic significance conditions must also be met.
